messages:
alex: heads up — saw a couple of OOMs on prod-nightly when routing large chat requests to the 'opt-13b' pool. repro traces attached in the profiler.

maria: can you paste the profiler snippet? is it allocator fragmentation or a single huge allocation? :eyes:

alex: snippet below — looks like many failed large allocs after a bunch of small frees (KV cache warmup). small freelist capacity ~420MB, attempted allocs ~1.2GB, then a big segmentation of small chunks so no contiguous region.

```
[2026-03-05 02:12:03] alloc(1.2GB) -> fail
free_list_summary: total_free=1.9GB, largest_contiguous=420MB
segment_policy=expandable_segments=true
recent_ops: kv_cache_prefill x 42, batch_concat kernels
```

ryan: hmm kv-prefill warmup + many concurrent streams tends to scatter the slab map. Did we have expandable_segments on? that can produce many small segments that don't coalesce well.

alex: yes current config on that pool is the default (expandable_segments: true, max_split_size_mb: 64, gc_threshold: 0.8).

maria: propose quick experiment: flip expandable_segments -> false for opt-13b pool, lower max_split_size_mb -> 32, and lower gc threshold to 0.6 so we trigger earlier compaction. that should create larger contiguous chunks and reduce failed large allocs.

sarah: sounds reasonable. two notes: 1) disabling expandable_segments can increase peak resident usage if we keep many large segments pinned. 2) smaller max_split_size_mb can hurt some kernels that rely on splitting large buffers — watch latency.

alex: agreed — we'll run with traffic shadow for 1 hour and collect peak_mem, contiguous_largest, OOM count, p50/p95 latency for generation.

infra-bot: deploy plan created: redwood-deploy/opt-13b/allocator-tweak-20260305 (shadow).

ryan: also add a config to try localized workspace pools for KV cache hot paths. idea: reserve a small per-stream workspace that grows up to X MB to avoid many tiny allocations during prefix copying. can be an opt-in knob: workspace_reserve_mb=64.

maria: good call. we'll test with workspace_reserve_mb=64 and a modified KV warmup that writes into the reserved buffer instead of malloc/free churn.

alex: experiment results (after 1hr shadow): contiguous_largest increased from avg 420MB -> 1.1GB, OOM count dropped from 7->0, p95 latency +2% (within SLO). memory peak +6%.

maria: that's promising. can you paste the reducer script we used to toggle knobs?

alex: sure — small example config we applied to the runtime agent: 

```
allocator:
  expandable_segments: false
  max_split_size_mb: 32
  garbage_collection_threshold: 0.6
  workspace_reserve_mb: 64

routing_policies:
  kv_prefill_concurrency_limit: 8
```

ryan: TL;DR — disabling expandable_segments + smaller split size + earlier GC + per-stream workspace reduced fragmentation and fixed the OOMs.

sarah: next steps: 1) run a 24h canary with same knobs on a small subset of traffic, 2) build a microbenchmark that simulates KV warmup + concurrent batch concat to reproduce locally, 3) add telemetry: largest_contiguous_histogram and fragment_count.

alex: I'll open a follow-up PR for the canary and the microbenchmark. will include perf regression checks for 5% latency.

maria: add note to run the kernel selection profiler for those runs — kernel dispatches sometimes pick a memory-heavy kernel under this config; want to ensure we didn't regress kernel choice.

alex: yep will capture kernel_choice traces. thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: canary scheduled -> redwood-canary/opt-13b/allocator-coalesce/24h (starts 2026-03-06 04:00 UTC).
